Use a local single-node Cassandra 4+ practice cluster and cqlsh. The SimpleStrategy keyspace below is only for that local lesson. These commands do not run in this site's SQLite playground.

blocks.title: Use a dedicated counter table

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: A primary key identifies a row and prevents duplicate key values. Related records can refer to that key.
A Cassandra counter supports increments with special rules. Repeating a retried increment may count it again.
`SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.

blocks.text: The stored counter increases by one each time the update is applied.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Counter retries need care because repeating an increment can count twice. Counter columns also have special schema restrictions.
